title: Father's conservatory career and Blanchin's early violin and jazz interest
summary: His father, Paris-trained, played and conducted in New Orleans theaters; George began violin at five and was drawn to jazz despite his father's dislike.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now you have a musical background, don't you? That's right, you told me. Your father.

Well that's correct. My father was a so-called legitimate musician. He studied and graduated from the Conservatory of Music in Paris, with very high honors and was considered a very fine musician. He played in the orchestras for his violinist at the old French Opera House. He conducted the orchestra at the Grunewald Cave, the Crescent and Tulane Theaters, which were legitimate theaters, the Dauphine Theater. That was before the Dauphine was burlesque. And of course he had many pupils in and around New Orleans, because he taught also. And of course my interest in music began when I was very young. I started studying violin at about the age of five. And became interested in jazz music not so very long afterwards, because I was hearing the Negro bands at the funerals and marching bands and whatnot. Much to the same displeasure of my father, who of course didn't like jazz and thought I should have no part of it.
